raw_response:
I have only 8 mu, so I cannot spread myself too thin. The wheat-maize land is still the main thing for feeding the family and keeping cash coming, so I will keep **6 mu** in wheat-maize double cropping, same as the way people around here do. I will leave **2 mu** for cotton. Cotton can bring money if the price is decent, but it takes more watching and more hand work, so I do not want too much of it when some people in my family are away working.

For wheat, I do not dare cut fertilizer too much. If wheat turns thin and yellow, the loss is big and I cannot make that back. I will do it the old way: base fertilizer before sowing, then one topdressing around jointing, and water a few times if the well water cost is still manageable. After wheat harvest in June, I will not waste time with heavy tillage on that land. The window is short, so I will clear the straw quickly and put maize in fast. For maize, I will not spend like a big farmer. I will use decent hybrid seed, one base dressing and one chasing fertilizer, and water only if rain is not enough. Cotton I will keep on the smaller piece. Cotton needs more hand work, but if I manage weeds and insects on time, it can still bring some cash. I would rather do a steady plan I can afford than chase a big yield and run short of money halfway through.
